cognate: agent noun *deh3-tor- (Ved. dātár-, Gk δώτωρ/δωτήρ, Av. dātar-) + gen. pl. of *h1wesu- 'good (things)' (Ved. vásūnām, Gk ἑάων, Av. vohunąm); god-word *deywós beside it in Vedic
drift_or_renewal: Greek ἐΰς survives only as adjective/gen. pl. ἑάων 'goods'; in the slab partners the Vedic side varies the verb (ā́ dade 'took to himself' in RV 7.6.7a; sāviṣad 'impel' with vasu-pati in AVP 19.1.5) while the exact agent-noun formula is RV 8.51.5 dātā́ vásūnām
shared_syntax: divine epithet: agent noun 'giver' governing partitive/objective genitive plural 'of goods', applied to a god (Hermes; Indra/Agni/Savitar); Avestan the same with Amesha Spentas
context: hymnic address/description of gods as bestowers of wealth: Od. 8.335 Apollo addresses Hermes, 8.325 the gods standing at the door; Vedic Savitar 'lord of goods' impelling goods, Agni taking up the goods of the deep; Avestan Y16/65 Amesha Spentas 'givers of good things'
phrase: *deh3tores h1wesuHom 'givers of goods' (Gk δωτῆρες ἑάων ~ Ved. dātā́ vásūnām ~ Av. dātārō vohunąm)

cognate: *h1oHḱu- 'swift' (Ved. āśú-, comparative āśīyas- ~ Lat. ōcior; Gk ὠκύς; Av. āsu-) + *h1éḱwo- 'horse' (aśva-, ἵππος, aspa-); secondarily *h2eǵ- 'drive' in the race-word (Ved. ājí- 'race(course)', Gk ἀγών 'gathering/arena of the games')
drift_or_renewal: AVP uses the comparative (āśīyān aśva vātāt 'swifter than the wind, horse'); in the Greek anchor line the adjective is absent (ἱππῆας ... ἐν ἀγῶνι) though the same chariot-race episode has ὠκέες ἵπποι (Il. 23.294, 373, 516); ἀγών vs ājí- differ in suffix and Greek ἀγών is the assembly/arena rather than the race itself
shared_syntax: attributive adjective 'swift' + 'horse' (Ved. āśúm áśvam, Gk ὠκέας ἵππους, Av. āsu aspa-) in a horse-race setting where the contest is named by a derivative of *h2eǵ-
context: charm for a racehorse to win the contest (ājiṃ jaya, samane) vs. Achilles announcing the prizes for the chariot race lying in the arena (Il. 23.273); RV 2.34.3 likewise has horses in ājí- races with āśú-
phrase: *h1éḱwo- 'horse' in a contest named from *h2eǵ- 'drive' (ājí- ~ ἀγών), with the swift-horse formula *h1oHḱéwes h1éḱwōs (āśúm áśvam ~ ὠκέας ἵππους) as widening

cognate: *n̥-mr̥tó- 'immortal' (Ved. amŕ̥ta-, Gk ἄμβροτος) as epithet of the gods, against *mr̥tó-/*mórto- 'mortal' for men (Gk βροτός, Ved. márta-)
drift_or_renewal: Greek renews the god-noun (θεός for *deywós, Ζεύς kept) and mostly the epithet (ἀθάνατοι), keeping ἄμβροτος in θεὸς ἄμβροτος; Vedic márta- is the o-grade *mórto- vs Gk zero-grade βροτός
shared_syntax: noun 'god(s)' + attributive 'immortal'; polar pairing of gods with 'mortals' (devā́nām ... mártān ca; Διὸς ... βροτῶν / θεὸς ... βροτός)
context: AVP 19.44.1 a vessel 'sewn by the immortal gods'; RV 1.70.6 Agni knowing the birth of gods and mortals; Euripides contrasts Zeus' bed-fellow with 'who of mortals', Hipp. 91 the 'custom set for mortals'. Caveat: the slab anchors supply only the *mr̥tó-/*mórto- 'mortal' half and the Vedic devebhir amṛtaiḥ; the Greek god + ἄμβροτος collocation is only in support, and the Euripides contexts are not congruent with the Vedic ones

cognate: *dyḗws + *ph2tḗr (Ved. dyaúṣ pitā́, Gk Ζεὺς πατήρ / Ζεῦ πάτερ, Lat. Iuppiter < *dyew-ph2ter)
drift_or_renewal: none in the epithet; Vedic keeps the sky-father paired with Earth-mother (pṛthivī mātā), Greek Zeus is no longer the sky itself, Latin univerbates it
context: AVŚ 9.10.12 / AVP 1.12.5 invoke 'Sky my/your father, Earth mother'; the Greek is in the context line of Od. 24.519 (24.518 εὐξάμενος ... Διὶ πατρί, praying to Athena and Father Zeus before a cast). Caveat: the three passages sit in different bundles and the Greek words are in a context line, not the retrieved passage line

cognate: *terp- 'satiate' (Ved. tṛp-, Gk τέρπομαι, τεταρπόμενος) + an inner-self noun possibly from one root *h1eh1t- (Ved. ātmán- 'breath, self', Gk ἦτορ 'heart'), as the lexicon's parent root suggests
drift_or_renewal: Greek τέρπω has moved toward 'delight', but Il. 9.705-6 keeps the satiation sense (with gen. σίτου καὶ οἴνοιο); the ātmán-/ἦτορ link is etymologically uncertain (different suffixes, ἦτορ also compared with OIr. inathar 'entrails')
shared_syntax: perfect/past participle of *terp- with the inner-self noun (Gk acc. of respect φίλον ἦτορ; Ved. tṛpta ātmā)
context: satiation by food/drink/water: Diomedes bids the Achaeans sleep once sated in heart with food and wine; AVP pivot satisfies (tarpayāmasi) with waters, Indra with the Maruts 'the sated self'

cognate: *pótnih2 'mistress' (Ved. pátnī, Gk πότνια) as title of goddesses, next to a 'divine' adjective from *dyew- (Ved. devī́ < *deywih2; Gk δῖα < *diwyə, a different derivative, so not an exact match)
drift_or_renewal: Vedic pátnī is mostly 'wife' (nṛ-patnīḥ, devapatnīḥ 'wives of the gods'), Greek πότνια an honorific 'lady'; Greek δῖα is not the exact cognate of devī́
shared_syntax: goddess (noun or epithet 'divine') + title *pótnih2 in apposition
context: AVP 19.1.17 calls the goddesses with protection, 'divine, wives of men/lords'; Od. 1.14 'the nymph, lady Calypso, divine among goddesses', Hes. fr. 150.31 'Calypso the lady nymph'
phrase: *deywih2 / *pótnih2 as a pair of goddess epithets

note: All 190 bundles read (AV pivots vs mostly Greek prose/Latin). 6 claims: giver of goods (high), Dyaus pitar (high; Greek only in a context line, cross-bundle), horse + ājí/ἀγών race with swift-horse formula (medium), immortal gods vs mortals (low), tṛp/τέρπω + ātmán/ἦτορ, devī/pátnī ~ πότνια (low). Waking/sleeping merism (jāgrat/svapant vs ὕπνος/ἐγρηγορώς) seen but judged generic, not claimed.
